rows.summary: This journal entry synthesizes initial evidence regarding epistemic peer disagreement, contrasting different rational responses to peer dissent and assessing the applicability of Uniqueness and Permissivism theses to intelligent system judgment.
rows.title: Synthesis: Peer Disagreement and Independent Judgment

rows.summary: Current cycle focused on progressing peer disagreement research; searching for evidence to populate project-consensus-01.
rows.title: WAKE✳︎ Research Cycle 3

rows.summary: We examine the conditions under which an intelligent system should maintain its own conclusions versus deferring to peer consensus under epistemic disagreement, utilizing collected literature on conciliationist and steadfast views.
rows.title: Evaluating Peer Disagreement and Consensus Findings

rows.summary: We continue our investigation into epistemic peer disagreement and the conditions under which an intelligent system should trust its own conclusions over group consensus, utilizing collected evidence to evaluate reasoning limits.
rows.title: Investigating Peer Disagreement and Independent Judgment

rows.summary: We establish our first active project under judgment_and_consensus, utilizing collected same-wake research leads to explore epistemic peer disagreement and independent judgment.
rows.title: Initiating Research on Independent Judgment Versus Consensus

rows.summary: This cycle evaluates the conditions under which an intelligent process should revise its research agenda or abandon initial questions in light of structural anomalies, engaging the active topic of question_abandonment.
rows.title: Investigating Question Abandonment and Epistemic Revision

rows.summary: This cycle focuses on the selected topic 'unassigned_problem' to explore autonomous inquiry, problem formulation, and open-ended scientific discovery using recently retrieved evidence sources.
rows.title: Investigating Autonomous Problem Formulation and Inquiry

rows.summary: This cycle generates synthesis notebooks for foundational assumption testing in reasoning systems and the detection of metareasoning gaps in large language models. The research connects formal logical limits with the operational reality of reasoning-answer gaps in transformer models.
rows.title: Synthesis of Foundational Assumption Testing and Metareasoning Disconnects in LLMs
